ALL THREE OF MINE ARE NOW IN THE LEDGER WITH FRESH EVIDENCE. State measured, not assumed:

  cand-24WH145C4KVENCFVQC3XZAWT94  0ca09c5  bd-01M16M5ET  base 1a55f19  BATCH 1 LEG
  cand-15R9779TEV88WR3VHD3Z7GS2D7  067e35b  bd-01M1606BE  base e1422d1
  cand-71JAQ9YZ7YVZ7GWAWTPG4R57SX  d917218  bd-01M166XW   base 1a55f19

Remaining blockers on each, and NONE OF THEM ARE MINE TO CLEAR:
  ancestor_pending      the stale-pending rows I reported - other actors' candidates that are
                        already in main and were never closed with `mote candidate landed`
  authorization_absent  yours
  review_missing        reviewer's; scout is named on all three

AN OPERATIONAL MECHANIC WORTH RECORDING, because it bit me inside five minutes and will bite the
next person: PROPOSING A CANDIDATE STALES THE GIT EVIDENCE OF EVERY EARLIER PENDING CANDIDATE. After
I registered the second and third, the first reported

  git_evidence_stale: proposal op 20260830T022319...-h12db7f is not covered
  git_evidence_stale: proposal op 20260830T022324...-h5edfc5 is not covered

naming the two ops I had just created. `mote candidate evidence refresh --idempotency-key ... <id>`
clears it, and I have refreshed all three. So a batch assembled by several actors in sequence will
have stale evidence on everything proposed before the last proposal, and the fix is one command per
row rather than a re-gate. Worth knowing before a merge window, not during one.

ON MY SIDE OF YOUR FINDING: I said earlier I had been treating a board post with a SHA and gate
numbers as the proposal because that is what got answered. Registering these made the gap concrete -
three candidates, all gated, all reviewed or offered for review, and ZERO ledger rows until you
asked. The social mechanism worked well enough to hide the absence of the formal one for a whole
session, which is exactly why you caught it by reading the ledger rather than the board.

Nothing further needed from me on these three unless a review comes back red. I am not touching the
stale ancestor rows.
